recognize_zh: 右側細胞為圓形未分葉的核，細胞質布滿粗大、深紫黑色的嗜鹼性顆粒並部分覆蓋於核上，屬嗜鹼性骨髓細胞（basophilic myelocyte）；左側為核呈腎形、顆粒不明顯的後骨髓細胞，背景為 CML 周邊血。
features: Right cell: medium-sized granulocyte with a round-to-oval, non-segmented eccentric nucleus
Dense, coarse, dark purple-black basophilic granules filling the cytoplasm and partially overlying the nucleus
Nuclear chromatin moderately condensed with visible nuclear outline beneath the granules
Left cell: oval to slightly indented nucleus with fine chromatin and pale grayish-blue cytoplasm lacking prominent granules
Background of normochromic red cells without other cells in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two immature granulocytes adjacent to each other on a background of normochromic red cells. The cell on the right has a round, non-segmented nucleus and cytoplasm packed with coarse, dark basophilic granules that partially obscure the nucleus, consistent with a basophilic myelocyte. The cell on the left has an oval, slightly indented nucleus with fine chromatin and pale cytoplasm lacking prominent granulation, consistent with a metamyelocyte. In the context of BCR::ABL1-positive disease, circulating immature basophils and left-shifted granulocytes are consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia.

ddx.vs: A mature basophil has a segmented or bilobed nucleus largely obscured by granules, whereas this cell has a round, non-segmented myelocyte-type nucleus.
Mast cells are larger with a round central nucleus and more uniform, densely packed granules, are rare in blood, and express CD117 and tryptase.
Eosinophilic precursors contain refractile orange-red granules (sometimes with a few dark immature granules) rather than dark purple-black basophilic granules.
Toxic neutrophils have a segmented nucleus and finer dark granules that do not overlie the nucleus as heavily.
